solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: See 5 down

parts.note: the clue at 5 down says the opera house's site is this word followed by the one at 28 across

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to the opera house clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 down clue is built from three unclued lights: the opera house's site is the London district whose first word goes here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Opera House stands in the Covent Garden district of London, whose first word fills this light.

clue.text: Horace, not Henry, could make a sheath

indicators.note: the remaining letters could make something new when rearranged, so they are reshuffled
'not Henry' tells us to leave out the letter standing for Henry

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man called Horace, rather than one called Henry, might fashion a sheath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes H from HORACE, leaving ORACE, and 'could make' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany an ocrea is a tubular sheath formed by stipules around a stem, as in the dock family.

clue.text: Typical EU destroyed trees

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are wrecked and rebuilt in a different order

explanation.surface: A grumble that the European Union has, as usual, wrecked the woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges the nine letters of TYPICAL and EU.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of eucalyptus, the gum trees native to Australia.

clue.text: Everybody's having to sit up around composer

indicators.note: the reversed word sits around the other piece, enclosing it
in a down clue 'up' means the word sit is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
everybody means all

explanation.surface: Everyone must stand for a composer's arrival, in a concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the word backwards because this is a down entry; 'around' then wraps it round the other piece. The 's of Everybody's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Tallis was a sixteenth-century English writer of church music.

clue.text: Old mother beginning to read wrote these verses

definitions.text: Old mother beginning to read wrote these verses

parts.words: Old mother beginning to read wrote these verses
parts.note: old gives O, mother gives MA and the first letter of read gives R: together they spell the poet Omar, who wrote the verses meant

explanation.surface: An elderly mother, just learning to read, has turned to writing poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening words build the name OMAR (O + MA + R); Omar Khayyam wrote these quatrains, so the clue reads 'Omar wrote these verses'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam is a famous collection of Persian quatrains, translated by FitzGerald.

clue.text: Its 19 across is 1 across, 28 across

parts.note: the clue says this building's site is Covent Garden, the London district where the national opera house stands

explanation.surface: A cross-reference saying where something is located.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill in the cross-references: its site is Covent Garden. COVENT GARDEN is a district of central London, home to the main opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Opera House, home of the Royal Opera and Royal Ballet, stands in Covent Garden.

clue.text: Bootless Orfeo composed in foreign tongue

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the word for a language

parts.note: bat is old army slang for the language of a foreign country, as in 'sling the bat'

indicators.note: the letters of the opera title are composed afresh, put into a new order

explanation.surface: Gluck's opera Orfeo, its performance useless, put into another language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' turns ORFEO into REFOO, which goes 'in' BAT. 'Bootless' looks like 'futile' but means without boots.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without boots or shoes on has bare feet.

clue.text: Character seen at 5 down lacking energy to portray this fair girl

indicators.note: lacking energy says the letter for energy is missing from the character's name

parts.note: Isolde, heroine of Wagner's Tristan und Isolde, is seen at the Royal Opera House
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An opera heroine, played without much vigour, as a pretty young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes E from ISOLDE. Isold the Fair is the Cornish princess of the Tristan legend.
explanation.definitionFit: In the legend Isold (Iseult) is called 'the Fair', a beautiful princess.

clue.text: Repulsive sailor's bristling

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor
horrent is a rare word meaning bristling or standing erect, like hairs

explanation.surface: An unpleasant seaman is in a prickly mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean detestable, causing disgust.

clue.text: Time to torture hen in railway vehicle

parts.note: the rack was an instrument of torture, and to rack is to torture
a laying hen is a layer

explanation.surface: A cruel scene of a hen being tormented aboard a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A track-laying machine running on rails puts down new railway line.

clue.text: Baron whose behaviour's 8 down, making expressions of impatience

definitions.meaning: Baron ... is the boorish, repulsive nobleman of Strauss's Der Rosenkavalier
och is a Scots and Irish exclamation of impatience, so these are several of them

explanation.surface: A nobleman's repulsive conduct makes people tut.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochs is the lecherous baron in Der Rosenkavalier; 'och' is an exclamation of irritation.

clue.text: Black removed top from tart one used at Wimbledon

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for a tart is taken away

parts.note: a tart is a prostitute, or call girl

explanation.surface: A dark pastry with its crust removed, eaten by someone at the tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed top from' takes C off CALL GIRL, leaving ALL GIRL. Wimbledon is the London tennis championship.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball girl retrieves loose balls for the players during a tennis match.

clue.text: It's felt agent accepted gold beforehand

indicators.note: beforehand puts the gold piece ahead of the letter for accepted

parts.note: a fed is an American federal agent
or is the heraldic word for gold
a. is an abbreviation for accepted, as on a bill of exchange

explanation.surface: An emotional agent took the gold in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'felt' poses as the past tense of feel but is the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft hat usually made of felt, so this is something made of felt.

clue.text: Redecorate bottom of eggshell

definitions.meaning: to ... a room is to refurbish it
Scots for the bottom or end of something, such as an eggshell

explanation.surface: Instructions to repaint the base of an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: To do up a house is to renovate it; Scots doup means a bottom or posterior end.

clue.text: Do it thus DC, and old true girl gets profit

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name from Latin vera, true
a profit is a gain

explanation.surface: An instruction for a performance, followed by an old-fashioned girl doing well.
explanation.walkthrough: DC is da capo, the musical instruction to go back to the start and play the music once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Da capo tells the player to repeat from the beginning, performing a second time.

clue.text: Punctual queen is found in 5 down…

parts.note: punctual means prompt, on time
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: A punctual monarch is spotted at the opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs on into the next clue: a prompter is one figure found in an opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompter feeds forgotten lines to performers from a box at the stage front in a theatre or opera house.

clue.text: Notice one or get behind

parts.note: a poster is a notice put up in public
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An instruction to spot one thing or else fall behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Posterior as a noun is the backside, the buttocks.

clue.text: Goes away as ballet's cancelled

parts.note: Swan Lake, the ballet, is cut to Swan, with the possessive giving the S
an event that is off has been cancelled

explanation.surface: A dancer departs because the performance has been called off.
explanation.definitionFit: To swan off is to leave casually or irresponsibly, wandering away.

clue.text: …clergyman with one jug is sometimes also present

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman
I is the Roman numeral for one
a ewer is a large jug

explanation.surface: A priest holding a jug turns up at the performance now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: This continues from the previous clue: a critic also attends at the opera house on some nights.
explanation.definitionFit: Critics attend performances at the opera house to write them up for papers.

clue.text: See 5 down

parts.note: the clue at 5 down begins 'Its 19 across is', asking for what the building has: the place it stands on

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to the opera house clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 down clue is built from three unclued lights; this one is the word for where a building stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A building's location, the ground it occupies, is its plot or position.

clue.text: Knife of SAS member's no good

parts.note: a para, a paratrooper, is taken as a member of the special airborne forces

explanation.surface: A blade carried by a special forces soldier is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A parang is a heavy Malay chopping knife, like a machete.

clue.text: Drivers having a jolly in French city

indicators.note: in says the marine's letters are placed in the city's name

parts.note: Caen is a city in Normandy
a jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: Motorists enjoying a spree in a city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer also names Bizet's opera, often staged at the Royal Opera House.
explanation.definitionFit: A carman is a driver of a cart or van, so carmen are such drivers.

clue.text: Formerly Portuguese Scotsman gets gold

parts.note: Mac is a nickname for a Scotsman
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A Scot who used to be Portuguese gets rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Macau was a Portuguese territory on the Chinese coast until 1999.

clue.text: Halévy's upset about measure that's celestial

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are wrapped about the printer's measure
the composer's name is upset, its letters knocked over into a new order

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter; Halévy is the French opera composer
an en is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: The composer Halévy is distressed by something heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges HALEVY to HEAVLY, which goes 'about' EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavenly and celestial both mean of the sky or of heaven.

clue.text: Rope encountered in fencing?

definitions.meaning: a long rein or rope used to train a horse in circles
a sudden forward thrust with the sword met in the sport of fencing

explanation.surface: A rope that turns up in a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' suggests a field boundary but is the sword sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge rein trains horses; a lunge is also a fencer's thrust.

clue.text: Refuse brandy in legendary Cornish King's audience

indicators.note: an audience is a hearing, so the king's name is heard rather than read

parts.note: King Mark of Cornwall is Isolde's husband in the Tristan legend

explanation.surface: Turning down a drink in the presence of a mythical monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' is not the verb but the noun: grape waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc is brandy distilled from the skins and pips left after grapes are pressed for wine.

clue.text: 'Eggspulsions'?

parts.note: a made-up word blending egg and expulsions, describing the release of eggs

explanation.surface: A jokey coinage for driving out eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Each such event is the release of an egg from the ovary.

clue.text: Remove wrapping from new hand warmer in rubber

indicators.note: in places the new piece and the hand warmer inside the tree's name

parts.note: ule is a Central American rubber tree, and its rubber
a muff is a fur tube for warming the hands

explanation.surface: Taking the wrapping off a new rubber handwarmer.
explanation.definitionFit: To unmuffle is to take off a muffling cover or wrap.

clue.text: See 5 down

parts.note: the clue at 5 down says the opera house's site is the word at 1 across followed by this one

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to the opera house clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 down clue is built from three unclued lights: this is the second word of the London district where the opera house stands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Opera House stands in the Covent Garden district of London, whose second word fills this light.
